title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: M is the category of graded modules over a graded ring S concentrated in degrees >= 0. The neighbouring pages concern divided-power de Rham complexes and Gamma_* constructions, but this page is pure graded-module bookkeeping. For an integer N', M_{N'} is the full subcategory of graded modules M with M_i = 0 for i < N', with inclusion i_{N'}.

Grothendieck writes down a chain of four adjoint functors q_{N'} -| i_{N'} -| tau_{N'} -| rho_{N'}:
(1) q_{N'}(M) = M / (submodule generated by the M_i, i < N'). This is the left adjoint of the inclusion, so M_{N'} is a localization (the bracket 'loc' over q, i).
(2) tau_{N'}(M) is the truncation M_{>=N'}. It is a submodule because S has no negative degrees. It is the right adjoint of i.
(3) rho_{N'} is the right adjoint of tau_{N'}, computed by Yoneda: rho_{N'}(P)_i = Hom_M(S(-i), rho P) = Hom_{M_{N'}}(tau_{N'}S(-i), P) = Hom^i(tau_{N'-i}S, P) = Hom_{M_{N'}}(T^{-i} tau_{N'-i} S, P).

Because tau o i = id, i is fully faithful (bracket 'pl. fid'). Hence its right-adjoint-of-right-adjoint rho is fully faithful too. So tau is also a localization (it is simultaneously a localization and a colocalization), which is the content of the marginal note under tau.

Second half: for N <= N' there are inclusions M_{N'} c M_N c M, with relative functors q_{N',N}, i_{N,N'}, tau_{N',N}, rho_{N,N'}. One has q_{N',N} = q_{N'}|M_N and tau_{N',N} = tau_{N'}|M_N. A chain of adjunction isomorphisms
Hom_{M_{N'}}(tau_{N'} i_N M, P) = Hom_M(i_N M, rho_{N'}P) = Hom_{M_N}(M, tau_N rho_{N'}P)
gives the boxed compatibility rho_{N,N'} = tau_N rho_{N'}.

Purpose: this is the transition system needed to pass to the limit N -> infinity. In that limit, colim_N Hom(S_{>=N}(-i), M) is Gamma_*(Proj S, M~), i.e. graded modules modulo 'eventually zero' (torsion) modules, presented as a direct system of localizations. Grothendieck presumably wants it in the setting of graded (divided-power) algebras for the de Rham complex material.
errors: No mathematical error. The line 'Hom_M(M, rho_{N'}P) = Hom_M(i_N M, rho_{N'}P)' silently identifies M with i_N M, a harmless abuse of notation.
Implicit hypothesis: S_j = 0 for j < 0, needed for tau_{N'}(M) to be a submodule. It is not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Quadruple of adjoints q -| i -| tau -| rho for the inclusion of graded modules vanishing below degree N'; i and rho fully faithful; tau both a localization and a colocalization
ideas.modern_name: adjoint quadruple / recollement-type data, (co)localization by truncation
ideas.where_published: related truncation arguments in EGA II §2.7 / EGA III §2 (Gamma_*, Serre's theorem)

ideas.what: Explicit right adjoint rho_{N'}(P)_i = Hom(tau_{N'-i}S(-i), P) and compatibility rho_{N,N'} = tau_N rho_{N'}
ideas.modern_name: Hom out of truncated S; the Gamma_* / Serre-type section functor as a colimit over truncations
ideas.where_published: closest is EGA II 2.7 / EGA III 2.3 (lim Hom(S_{>=n}, M))

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard adjunction bookkeeping for degree truncations of graded modules, a preparation for the Proj / Gamma_* limit. Nothing here is new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The label over the top bracket reads 'pl. fid' (pleinement fidèle), not 'adj. fid'. The bracket appears to span i_{N'}, tau_{N'}, rho_{N'}, marking i and rho as fully faithful.

The marginal note under tau_{N'} begins 'loc. ...' and continues roughly 'catégories obtenues ... équivalentes'. It plausibly says that tau is also a localization (two localizations giving equivalent categories). The machine reading 'und[?] et [?] ... c'y a rien' is unreliable.
The isolated symbol to the right of rho_{N'} on the top line is a lone 'rho' (or 'f'), not part of the formula.
The word before the boxed formula is 'donc'.
